title: Allocation is not utilization: two real GPUs, one working, one held by an idle notebook
purpose: On the two real GPUs, start a pod that runs the CUDA n-body benchmark in a loop and a 'notebook' pod that holds a GPU and does nothing. Both GPUs are allocated; read what DCGM measures on each, and how the accounting service classifies them.

steps.display: kubectl apply -f real-gpu-pods.yaml   # trainer-busy (n-body loop), notebook-idle (sleep)

steps.output:
POD             NODE                                         PHASE     GPU
notebook-idle   ip-10-86-25-255.us-east-2.compute.internal   Running   1
trainer-busy    ip-10-86-52-153.us-east-2.compute.internal   Running   1

steps.display: DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL_RATIO from each DCGM exporter pod (kubectl get --raw .../pods/<exporter>:9400/proxy/metrics)
accounting: GPU-minutes of the real pool over the last 90 s, by category

checks.description: both GPUs are allocated, on two different nodes: 100% allocation
checks.because: Each pod requests one nvidia.com/gpu; the device plugin assigns each a whole device.

checks.description: DCGM measures the trainer's GPU above 50% busy and the notebook's at 0%
checks.because: Allocation counts requests; DCGM counts the GPU's own activity.

checks.description: the accounting service puts half of the allocated GPU-minutes in busy and half in allocated_idle
checks.because: It matches DCGM's per-pod utilization to the pod that holds each GPU.
